findings.problem: The trick says ich is me, but ich means I and the German for me is mich, which could confuse the learner.
findings.fix: trick: SICH rhymes with ich (I): ich is I, and sich is himself, herself or themselves.

back.target: himself, herself, itself, themselves (third-person reflexive pronoun; also yourself with formal Sie)
back.example: He is looking forward to the weekend.

note: The prompt alone (Er wäscht sich) already gives only sich, so the hint isn't strictly needed but is harmless; the example uses reflexive sich with sich freuen auf, where English has no himself.
